key_insight: Microencapsulated beadlets are multiparticulate drug delivery systems that use polymer matrices or core–shell coatings to precisely tune stability, protection, and release profile.
engineering_relevance: The paper is relevant to coating microstructure and process engineering because beadlet performance depends on material selection, coating uniformity, and controllable manufacturing methods.
method: Review of formation routes: solvent evaporation, coacervation, fluid-bed coating, extrusion–spheronization, ionotropic gelation, spray drying/congealing, melt processes, microfluidics, and electrohydrodynamic atomization.
Comparison of polymer classes, including natural, semi-synthetic, synthetic, and biodegradable systems, for encapsulation efficiency and release control.
Assessment of critical quality attributes such as particle size, morphology, porosity, drug loading, swelling, compatibility, and release kinetics.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates evaluation through standard formulation and performance metrics, especially encapsulation efficiency, solid-state characterization, and in vitro drug release testing.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is maintaining reproducible large-scale manufacturing, especially coating uniformity and process control during scale-up.
